Having offered [the Vaiśvadeva oblations], he gives what remains to the one who has won; having given according to his faith and assigned it, and having offered the Vaiśvakarman oblations, he offers the *paryāptis* on the Āhavanīya fire. He does not take the *vasatīvarī* waters behind [the altar]. The midday pressing concludes straightforwardly; the third pressing concludes straightforwardly. This is the *sarvastoma*.

Regarding the *atirātra*: "O Brahman, we shall set forth," he says; having performed the *anuyāja* offerings, he offers the *svaru*. Then, having proceeded with the *hāryojana* offerings, they proceed with the *apsuṣoma* offerings. Then, having gone back westward, they perform the *patnīsaṃyāja* sacrifices with the tails. When he cuts portions from the tails for Agni Gṛhapati, that [portion] is from this iron vessel.

Having brought a splinter from the *kamaṇḍalu* vessel, they smear wood that has been anointed with the splinter beneath the hand; having performed the *patnīsaṃyāja* offerings, they go forward to the east.

He recites six verses containing the word *ṛgmīya*; he offers three *yajus*-formulas; they join together the tenth [verse] beginning with *āyurdāḥ*; they take up the *avabhṛtha* (concluding bath) materials: a small wooden ladle (*sruva*), a large sacrificial ladle (*sruc*), a vessel for clarified butter (*ājyasthālī*), clarified butter, a cake on ten potsherds for Varuṇa, garments for each person, and an iron water-pot (*kamaṇḍalu*). They bring this man who is white, leprous, bald, and tawny-eyed.

44. Then they cause either a boat or an elephant to be stationed at the southern pond. Having approached the *cātvāla* pit, they go down to the purificatory bath (*avabhṛtha*) in the southern pond with these three sections: "The vigorous one has stepped across with strides," "The vigorous one has stepped upon the earth," and "Those paths of Savitṛ which are ancient. Having arrived there, he offers the *avabhṛtha* oblation of the *adhvara* sacrifice with the verse: "The face of Agni... and so forth.

"He entered"—thus [it is said]. Then he offers the *avabhṛtha* (concluding bath) oblation for Agni with the verse, "To the ocean, the one who knows the way. Then he offers the *avabhṛtha* oblation for the Aśvamedha with the formula, "Homage to the King, homage to Varuṇa. The remainder is the ritual bathing; that [bathing] proceeds from this [point].

Having drawn out a splinter from an iron water-pot, he offers it upward to ward off evil; some indeed offer it downward, but he should rather offer it on both sides. Striking with a piece of wood, he makes the offering: "To Death, svāhā!"

"To Death, svāhā!"—thus [he offers]; "To Effort, svāhā!"—thus [he offers]. There are ninety oblations; those eleven make one hundred and one. Then they board either a boat or an elephant; then this white, moist one goes before them.

When they come to bathe there, he submerges him who is about to submerge; for one who is being submerged, if a whirlpool should arise over his head, then he offers these *tejanī* oblations with the words: “To Jumbaka, svāhā!”—thus.

He steps aside to the right and hands over his water-pot (*kamaṇḍalu*). Having received it, he steps aside to the right in such a way that he is properly instructed. Then, having given him a hundred oxen and a hundred [pieces of gold], he said:
“O Kṣattṛ, do this for him, then lead him away; do not let him dwell within my domain. They bathe at the Pratigādha; having bathed, they emerge. [End of section 11.29]

Having performed the *udayanīya* offering, he immolates a barren cow dedicated to Mitra and Varuṇa; for that [cow], there are nine verses addressed to Sūrya as the *praüga* recitation, which are to be recited loudly.

[He gives the call] for the offering to Mitra and Varuṇa aloud, and for the offerings to Sūrya in a low voice, just as for a single one. Having offered the omenta of those [animals] and having performed the ritual purification (*mārjana*), he goes westward and, following the procedure for the *pātnīvata* cup, having raised the *pātnīvata* [cup], they immolate these animals upon it: a spotted goat, a *kikidīvi* bird, and a *vidīgaya*. Thus [they do].

Having released the Varuṇa cake on one potsherd after it has been encircled by fire, they offer the animal-cake offerings (*paśupuroḍāśa*); [according to M: they proceed with the two animal-cake offerings]. There is a cake for Mitra-Varuṇa on one potsherd, or nine, or one for Sūrya;

these follow them, as do the oblations for the Devikās and the goddesses. He calls for the *āśrāvaṇa* loudly for the offering to Mitra-Varuṇa, but in a low voice for the offerings to Sūrya. As for a single [offering], so too are the animal-cake offerings accompanied by the *praiṣa* (directions): "Recite! and "Sacrifice! (*anubrūhi*, *yaja*).

For the other oblations of beef, he offers them silently before the *puroḍāśa-sviṣṭakṛt* with the verse, "May the wind, the bringer of bliss, blow upon the cows. The *praiṣa* is the same, the *sviṣṭakṛt* is the same, and the *iḍā* is the same; before the *paśu-sviṣṭakṛt*, he performs the *sannatīs*.

Having offered the *anūyāja* oblations with the formula, “To Agni, the equal one, svāhā,” and having performed the *patnīsaṃyāja* offerings, he offers the *mābhava* oblations before the *samiṣṭayajus*. Then, after the *samiṣṭayajus*, he offers twenty-four *anubhava* oblations with the formula, “By means of Agni, he experienced heat. Having proceeded with the *ṛjupaśu* animals and having performed the *yajñavāstu* rite, he concludes the sacrifice (*udavasāna*). And then he says this very thing.

Then, on the following day, which was the wedding day, they erected a large sacrificial post (*yūpa*) and immolated these animals upon it: one for Agni, one for Indra-Agni, and one for the Aśvins. Having offered their omenta and performed the ritual purification (*mārjana*), they proceeded.

They offer the *paśupuroḍāśa* cakes; these are followed by the *mṛgāreṣṭi*: "To Agni Amhomuc, an eight-potsherd [cake]"—this is their *yājyā* and *anuvākyā*: "I meditate upon Agni, the first, the wise one... that we, O youngest one, may [attain] among men... [as previously recited].

As it is said: "O Vasus, that which... and "The cow, indeed... are the two *saṃyājyā* verses. The animal-cake offerings (*paśupuroḍāśa*) are accompanied by formal calls (*praiṣa*), with the calls being "Recite! and "Sacrifice! For the other oblations, he offers the splendors of sacred knowledge (*brahmavarcasa*) silently before the *puroḍāśa-sviṣṭakṛt* offering.

"O Brahman, may a Brāhmaṇa endowed with Vedic splendor (*brahmavarcas*) be born! With this same *praiṣa*-formula, the *sviṣṭakṛt* offering is performed; the *iḍā* is common [to all]; he gives two hundred oxen yoked for transport to the lute-players (*vīṇāgāthin*), and having proceeded with the straight-sacrificed animals (*ṛjupaśu*), having performed the rites for the sacrificial site (*yajñavāstu*), he concludes the sacrifice. Then, on the day after the wedding—or on the following day, or even if it has not yet occurred—they offer twelve *brahmaudana* oblations; for these, there are indeed golden plates (*rukmā*).
There are the under-spreading and the sprinkling; these very four great officiating priests consume them, and thus [the portions] for them are four.

He gives either four thousand [cows], or he obtains one hundred *pala* for each. This indeed is the *Śākha* full-moon day; on that day, he sacrifices three tawny ones of the spring season, three dappled ones of the summer season in the heat, three speckled ones in the rains, and three spotted ones of the autumn season in the fall.

In winter, three [animals] with dappled thighs; in the cold season, three smeared with fat; and in the dewy season, three with hair on their chests. When the year has returned, the Aśvamedha is completed for the sake of the year; the Aśvamedha is completed. The ninth Anuvāka. The Prapāṭhaka named Aśvamedha is finished.
